decisive_items: abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant
Ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis

Computed tomography of the abdomen revealed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant, causing partial luminal obliteration and edema on the anterolateral aspect of the cecum
response.rationale: R5 aligns with the classic migratory pain, ultrasound plastron appendicitis, and CT findings of cecal edema with a luminal linear lesion (likely fecalith), while R1 only uses the CT linear lesion without supporting clinical or ultrasound features; R4 is contradicted by denied GI symptoms and imaging findings.

rejected.why: Denied anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation; imaging and CT findings are not consistent with gastroenteritis.
